races.paceDynamic: Hey Havana is the sole confirmed front runner in this 14-runner field, meaning he can dictate a comfortable tempo without early pressure. The lack of other pace angles will allow Hey Havana to bowl along at sustainable fractions through the early stages. With 13 hold-up horses behind him, the race will develop into a classic scenario where the field bunches up turning for home before a late cavalry charge. This pace shape strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can avoid the traffic problems that will inevitably engulf the large pack of hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hey Havana Controls All
scenarios.trigger: If Hey Havana gets uncontested fractions and maintains his kick
scenarios.body: The lone pace-setter can dictate ideal splits and prove hard to peg back when the field finally mounts their challenge. His prominent style and recent second at this trip suggests he can exploit this tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Charge Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too slow and favours a strong closer
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get their perfect scenario with a crawling pace that sets up a sprint finish. Quality closers like Thestral and Inferno can unleash their finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Benefits Outsiders
scenarios.trigger: If the large field creates significant interference in the straight
scenarios.body: The 13 hold-up horses create a wall of traffic that catches out fancied runners. Lightly-weighted horses with clear runs can capitalize on others' misfortune.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Suits All
scenarios.trigger: If Hey Havana sets an honest but not excessive gallop
scenarios.body: The pace allows both the leader to stay on and closers to finish effectively. Form horses can settle into their preferred positions and battle on merit.

watchPoints.text: Hey Havana must be watched closely in the early stages - if he gets soft fractions he becomes very dangerous as the sole pace angle
Watch for traffic problems turning into the straight with 13 hold-up horses all needing room at the same time
Thestral's fitness after 34 days off needs monitoring, but Oisin Murphy's booking suggests connections expect a big run
Supreme Dancer and Space Moon carrying significantly less weight could be overpriced given their recent form improvements
Track the early pace closely - if it's too steady it will set up a cavalry charge that could catch out the leader

runners_data.name: Rajapour

runners_data.name: Flying Fletcher
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who may press Roaring Ralph early but form figures suggest he's not quite at his best currently

runners_data.name: Roaring Ralph
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner in red-hot form with strong recent wins who can dominate if getting soft splits

runners_data.name: Great Blasket
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with decent form who benefits from the tactical nature but needs to overcome a moderate recent effort

runners_data.name: Popeye Doyle
runners_data.note: Closing style suits but poor trainer strike-rate and 29-day break raise questions about immediate readiness

runners_data.name: Sunny Orange
runners_data.note: Bottom-weight hold-up horse who gets significant weight relief but form figures suggest he's outclassed at this level

races.paceDynamic: Roaring Ralph will set the early pace from his prominent position, likely accompanied by Flying Fletcher who also races prominently. With only two natural pace-setters in a 7-runner field, the early gallop should be measured and sustainable rather than testing. The large contingent of hold-up horses (Garden Oasis, Rajapour, Great Blasket, Popeye Doyle, Sunny Orange) will track behind in what becomes a tactical affair. This controlled tempo strongly favours the hold-up specialists who can unleash finishing kicks in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tactical Hold-Up Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Roaring Ralph and Flying Fletcher set a steady pace without pressure
scenarios.body: The moderate gallop allows the large group of closers to conserve energy and produce telling late runs. Garden Oasis and Rajapour, both proven at this level with strong finishing kicks, benefit most from this patient scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If Roaring Ralph gets an uncontested lead and kicks clear
scenarios.body: His excellent recent form (211121) and the lack of genuine pace pressure allows him to dictate terms throughout. Flying Fletcher may chase but cannot match the leader's current momentum.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If both prominent runners go too slowly early and get swamped
scenarios.body: The tactical nature backfires as all the hold-up horses converge simultaneously in a blanket finish. The lightest-weighted Sunny Orange benefits from his 14lb advantage over the top-rated horses.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stronger Pace Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Flying Fletcher challenges Roaring Ralph for the early lead
scenarios.body: The unexpected dual creates a faster tempo that stretches the field and tests stamina reserves. Proven stayers like Garden Oasis can capitalise on the honest gallop.

watchPoints.text: Roaring Ralph breaking fast and establishing a clear early lead could prove decisive given his current purple patch
Garden Oasis and Rajapour both switching off too much in the steady gallop and getting caught flat-footed when the sprint begins
Flying Fletcher's early positioning - whether he sits off Roaring Ralph or attempts to pressure the leader changes the complexion
The weight disparity between top-rated Garden Oasis/Rajapour (140lbs) and Sunny Orange (126lbs) in a tactical finish
Great Blasket bouncing back from his last disappointing run when returning to this more suitable distance

races.paceDynamic: Newyorkstateofmind will be the sole pace-setter in this nine-runner field, with all other runners adopting hold-up tactics from midfield back. This creates a perfect scenario for the leader to control fractions without early pressure, likely dictating moderate splits before quickening. With eight hold-up horses bunched behind, the finish will be a cavalry charge where traffic problems and positioning become crucial. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners and those with proven finishing kicks from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Newyorkstateofmind gets soft fractions and kicks clear turning for home
scenarios.body: The veteran controls every call without pressure and uses his class edge to repel late challengers. Hold-up horses get in each other's way in a bunched finish behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Charge Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too slow and hold-up horses get clear runs
scenarios.body: The lack of early speed allows closers to unleash devastating finishing kicks in the final furlong. Newyorkstateofmind gets swamped by multiple challengers with superior turn of foot.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field stays bunched and multiple hold-up horses get blocked
scenarios.body: A messy finish develops where positioning matters more than ability, creating upset potential. Horses with room to maneuver or rail runs benefit while others are shuffled back.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Special
scenarios.trigger: If Newyorkstateofmind goes too slow early and stops suddenly
scenarios.body: The leader sets crawling fractions then hits the wall, allowing any hold-up horse with a clean run to capitalize. The winner emerges from the pack with the best late acceleration.

watchPoints.text: Newyorkstateofmind getting uncontested lead - if James Sullivan can dictate slow fractions, the leader becomes extremely dangerous
Traffic problems in home straight - with eight hold-up horses bunched together, several contenders could get blocked for crucial runs
Desert Master and Captain Cess positioning - both need clear runs to unleash finishing kicks and draw away from the pack
Headgear changes on Blackjack and Newyorkstateofmind suggesting both connections expect improved efforts
Pinpoint's fitness after 142-day break - long absence makes him vulnerable despite previous course success

races.paceDynamic: With all nine runners showing hold-up styles and no confirmed front-runner, this race will drift into a crawling pace early as jockeys look for someone else to make the running. Golden Prosperity and Crafty Spirit may be reluctantly pushed forward given their recent form patterns, but neither wants to lead from the front. The inevitable slow gallop will turn this 5½f contest into a cavalry charge from the 2f pole, creating a bunched sprint finish where positioning and a clear run become crucial. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with tactical speed who can quicken from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Messy Slow-Burn Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If nobody wants to lead and the pace crawls for 3 furlongs
scenarios.body: The field will be tightly bunched turning for home, creating traffic problems and favouring horses drawn well or with smart jockeys. Fresh runners like Crafty Spirit and Happier who can quicken late will benefit from the tactical nature.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Golden Prosperity Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Golden Prosperity gets an uncontested lead from his good draw
scenarios.body: With his recent win and proven ability on good ground, he could steal a march while others are still organising behind. The lack of early pace pressure would allow him to dictate terms and prove hard to peg back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Sprint Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is suicidal early with multiple horses going forward
scenarios.body: Those who settle last of all will have the best chance as the early leaders capitulate in the final furlong. Jason Hart on Solar Biricz and Tom Eaves on Angel Of England will benefit from maximum cover and a strong finishing kick.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Bishop's Glory Timing
scenarios.trigger: If Bishop's Glory gets the perfect trip from Andrea Pinna's claim
scenarios.body: His consistent recent form and the 7lb claim could be decisive if he times his run to perfection from mid-division. The South African form around similar types looks solid for this grade.

watchPoints.text: Golden Prosperity if he jumps out fast and gets an easy lead - his recent win and good going record make him dangerous with no pace pressure
Watch for traffic problems in the home straight with all nine runners likely to be tightly bunched turning for home
Andrea Pinna's 7lb claim on Bishop's Glory could be the difference in a tight finish between horses of similar ability
Crafty Spirit and Happier both come here fresh off recent good runs and could benefit most from the likely sprint finish
Solar Biricz with Jason Hart having only a 9-day break might be sharper than rivals who have been off longer

races.paceDynamic: With no natural front-runners and all ten horses showing hold-up tendencies, this will develop into a crawling pace early with the field bunched together through the first half-mile. The lack of early pace will see horses like Heart Sign, Bradbury and Clear Above positioned closer to the pace than usual, but none wanting to commit to making the running. This sets up a frantic sprint finish over the final 2-3 furlongs where positioning and a clear run will be crucial. The race shape strongly favours horses with tactical speed and finishing kick rather than one-paced plodders.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Crawling Pace Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If no horse takes them along early creating a muddling tempo
scenarios.body: The field will arrive at the 2f pole in a wall with minimal galloping done, turning it into a 2f dash where class and finishing kick separate them. Horses like Bradbury and Heart Sign with recent winning form and tactical speed will thrive in this finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Moderate Early Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Heart Sign or Clear Above get pushed forward to create some early pace
scenarios.body: A more honest gallop will stretch the field slightly but still set up a sprint finish where the classier animals can show their superior turn of foot. The better-handicapped horses with proven finishing ability will dominate.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Messy Tactical Affair
scenarios.trigger: If jockeys get involved in early positioning battles creating stop-start fractions
scenarios.body: The race becomes disjointed with horses getting shuffled back and blocked, making it a lottery where the best-positioned horse at the 2f pole wins regardless of ability. Those drawn well or getting early position will have decisive advantages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Injection of Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Billy Garritty on Clear Above decides to inject pace from halfway to utilise stamina
scenarios.body: This creates a more genuine test where horses need both pace and stamina to win, potentially catching out some pure sprinters. The most progressive horse with proven stamina will benefit from this stronger tempo.

watchPoints.text: Rugby Union and Here Comes Louie both returning from lengthy breaks with known finishing issues - avoid if pace collapses
Princess Coco and Clova Royale both have warning flags for fading in the finish which could be crucial in a sprint
Watch for early positioning of Heart Sign and Clear Above as they may get forced closer to pace than ideal
Jockey tactics will be crucial with Kevin Stott on Bradbury and Billy Garritty on Clear Above both experienced at getting good positions
The 5lb claim for Rhys Elliott on Princess Coco may not be enough to overcome the mare's limitations in this grade
